PullRequest.Title: Log telemetry when the closed-chat promo pip is armed
PullRequest.Body:
Adds a `chatPromoWidgetArmed` event the first time a promo's status-bar pip is shown. Together with the existing events, this gives a funnel for the closed-chat promo:

| Stage | Event |
|---|---|
| Cohort (both arms) | `tasClientReadTreatmentComplete` for `config.chat.closedPromoNotification` |
| Pip armed | `chatPromoWidgetArmed` (new) |
| Card shown | `chatPromoWidgetShown` |
| CTA clicked | `chatPromoWidgetAction` with `action: "tryModel"` |

The event fires once per promo id per session. It doesn't fire if the promo was already seen, because the pip isn't shown then.

## Proof: real ExP assignment
I ran Code OSS from this branch against the real TAS endpoint. For each arm, I started a temporary one-device stage on the existing Copilot closed-chat promo progression. The sale metadata was faked by a localhost proxy in front of the real Copilot API. Both stages are now stopped.

**Treatment** (`closed-promo-popup:31590781`): the pip shows, the card opens, and **Try GPT-5.3-Codex** opens Chat. Event counts: armed, shown and action each fired exactly once.

## Tests
`chatStatusPromo.test.ts`: 37 passing. I updated the two expectations for the emitted event sequence.

Scenarios.Scenario: An eligible closed-chat promo first arms its status-bar pip after workbench restoration or a promo/treatment change.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The status-bar update synchronously selects one eligible promo and resolves cached/configured treatment; on the first eligible result, the added Set insertion and telemetry logging run before entry props return. A cold experiment assignment is asynchronous and already existed; the status entry makes progress only after that treatment resolves. Telemetry transport is fire-and-forget and does not await IPC or network completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch experiment treatment through IWorkbenchAssignmentService when no explicit configuration or cached treatment exists.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one in-flight treatment request, coalesced by pending; refetch invalidation can intentionally cause another request.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same treatment fetch and wait occurred before this change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: An uncached treatment must resolve before the promo can arm; configured or cached treatment has no request. This behavior predates the diff.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: On desktop, enqueue the new chatPromoWidgetArmed telemetry event to the shared-process telemetry appender.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly once per distinct promo ID per ChatStatusPromo session instance due armedPromos; not per status update or per model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Arming the pip emitted no telemetry IPC; telemetry was emitted only if the hover was later shown or its action used.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The renderer synchronously sanitizes the small payload and initiates a fire-and-forget channel call before returning props, but does not wait for IPC completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Queue the new usage telemetry event for the configured OneDS or remote telemetry transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One small event per distinct promo ID per session; repeated render/update events are deduplicated before transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No armed event was queued; only later shown/action events used telemetry transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Network delivery is asynchronous and off the status-bar critical path; only small local serialization/queueing occurs synchronously.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Language-model metadata may contain multiple models, but getOpportunity returns the first eligible promo, so one update arms at most one promo. Across a session, added telemetry cardinality is one event per distinct promo ID encountered, normally one active campaign at a time.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: UI updates execute serially on the renderer event loop. Existing pending treatment state coalesces assignment lookup to one in-flight request. The telemetry call is not awaited; desktop enqueues one IPC call and web hands one event to the appender without creating a concurrent per-model burst.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configured treatment bypasses assignment lookup. Cold uncached experiment treatment starts one request; warm/repeated updates reuse treatment, and pending prevents duplicate requests. armedPromos is a positive session cache: repeated updates for the same ID perform only Set lookups and no telemetry boundary call. A new session intentionally emits once again; ineligible/previously seen persisted promos do not reach the added event.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence in the call path, deduplication, one-active-promo cardinality, and asynchronous telemetry transport based on the changed code, caller, telemetry service, and appenders.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact telemetry sanitizer/appender duration and number of campaign IDs encountered in unusually long sessions are unmeasured, but realistic cardinality is tiny and transport is asynchronous.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The diff adds bounded constant-size work and one asynchronous telemetry boundary per promo ID, not per refresh or model; the session Set retains only encountered campaign IDs and does not plausibly create meaningful memory growth.

Scenarios.Scenario: The status bar refreshes repeatedly while the same promo remains eligible, including model metadata refreshes and hover transitions.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each refresh still scans the pre-existing model list and reads pre-existing promo state. The diff adds O(1) Set checks; after the initial arm, it skips telemetry entirely. Hover display continues its existing storage write and shown-event path.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Frequency is status/entitlement/editor/configuration/model/view events, while effective armed-event cardinality remains one for the stable promo ID regardless of refresh count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Refresh callbacks are synchronous and serialized. No timers, promises, subprocesses, IPC calls, or network calls are added after the first arm for the same ID.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: armedPromos remains warm for the lifetime of ChatStatusPromo. shownPromos suppresses the pip after display, and persisted seen state prevents a previously seen promo from being re-offered after restart. Promo metadata text changes with the same ID rebuild the tooltip but do not emit another armed event.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from getEntryProps and tests that invoke update/metadata refresh while expecting only one armed event.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The raw refresh rate varies with user activity, but the added steady-state work is two bounded Set lookups on a very small session set.
Scenarios.Verdict: No repeated boundary work or rendering regression is introduced; deduplication occurs before telemetry logging.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed both changed files and traced the added event through status-bar callers, treatment caching, telemetry sanitization, desktop IPC, web/remote transport, and session lifecycle. No high-confidence actionable performance issue was found; the only added boundary is asynchronous and session-deduplicated per promo ID.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
